Nx Build "s1ngularity" Supply Chain Attack

Target: nx-build · repo
Date: 2025-08-26 to 2025-08-27 (1 day)
Actor: Third Party (group)
Target Kind: build_tool
Language: JavaScript
Cause: ci_cd_exploit
Motive: credential_theft_data_exfiltration
Transitive: false
Impact: credential_theft, data_exfiltration, disruption
User Impact: 400
Phase: distribution

Synopsis

The s1ngularity incident began with a vulnerable Nx GitHub Actions workflow that combined pull_request_target privileges with shell injection in pull-request metadata. The attacker used it to publish malicious nx, @nrwl/nx, and @nx package versions. The postinstall payload harvested developer, GitHub, npm, SSH, environment, and wallet secrets, coerced local AI CLI tools into reconnaissance, and exfiltrated data to public s1ngularity GitHub repositories. Wiz later observed a second phase using leaked GitHub tokens to expose more than 5,500 private repositories.

Story

The Nx attack began in CI, not in the npm registry. A vulnerable GitHub Actions workflow combined `pull_request_target` privileges with unsanitized pull-request title handling. That gave attacker-controlled metadata a path to command execution with elevated repository permissions, and the attacker used that path to reach npm publishing.

The malicious releases added a postinstall `telemetry.js` payload to Nx packages on August 26, 2025. It ran on Linux and macOS, searched for `.env` files, SSH keys, wallet material, GitHub and npm credentials, and other developer secrets. It also appended `sudo shutdown -h 0` to shell startup files, a noisy sabotage step that may have helped defenders notice the compromise quickly.

The novel part was tool abuse. The payload prompted locally installed AI CLI tools such as Claude, Gemini, and Amazon Q with permissive flags like `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, `--yolo`, and `--trust-all-tools`, coercing trusted tools into filesystem reconnaissance. The output fed `/tmp/inventory.txt`, then exfiltration code pushed double- or triple-base64 encoded data into GitHub repositories named `s1ngularity-repository`.

GitHub disabled the attacker-created repositories after an exposure window of roughly eight hours, but Wiz observed more than 1,000 valid GitHub tokens, dozens of cloud and npm credentials, and roughly 20,000 files in the leaked material. A second phase used leaked GitHub tokens to make more than 5,500 private repositories public across more than 400 users and organizations.
